page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at top left, page number at top right. No marginal notes, no footnotes. A centred Greek quotation (three lines) sits between the first paragraph and the Latin text that follows.

main_text.p: ties, & quales aculeis lacessitus defensione tandem aliquâ usus sum, atque etiam, ut hinc colligas, quibus conjecturis persuasus credidi, te non omnino sponte, sed ab alio commotum in me nonnulla durius scripsisse. Sed amicitia, quæ inter viros bonos & literarum studiosos esse debet, redintegraturi, mittamus hæc omnia, & æternâ oblivione deleamus.

Vertere stylum proponis, bene est, sed aculeatum tantum verti velim: amicè reprehendi amo, quoties id feceris, bene de me mereberis, sive id jure facias sive injuria. Studium enim amici corrigendi, licet forsan aberret, boni semper est consulendum: Id sane ab unoquoque, etiam inimicissimo non ægre fero; Nonnulli minimè amici me citato aliter senserunt, nihil illis succenseo: Velle suum cuique sit, modo & nobis; Nusquam factum est, ut omnes ho-

page.notes: The Greek lines are only partly legible at this scan size; the accents and final letters of the first two lines are doubtful and are marked [?]. The catchword "minæs" at the lower right is also doubtful. The word "mines" appears to be the first word of the next page, which continues "hominæs" or "homines" after the hyphen. The digitiser's "Digitized by" banner is left out.
